text:
**For a MacBook Air, 30W is the minimum, and 65-70W is the sweet spot if you want fast charging.**

- **Minimum:** Apple lists 30W as the minimum wattage to charge the current 13-inch MacBook Air ([Apple tech specs](https://images.apple.com/tm/macbook-air/specs/)).
- **Apple's recommended adapters** for models from 2022 on are the 30W (13-inch only), 35W Dual USB-C, 67W, or 70W USB-C adapters. The 40W Dynamic adapter with 60W Max also works when paired with a USB-C charge cable ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)).
- **What comes in the box:**
  - The 13-inch M5 Air includes a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/126320)).
  - The 13-inch M4 Air includes a 30W adapter with the 8-core GPU, or a 35W dual-port adapter with the 10-core GPU ([Apple Support](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/122209)).
- **Fast charging:** You need a 70W or higher USB PD power source ([Apple tech specs](https://images.apple.com/macbook-air/specs/)).
- **Third-party chargers:** Any USB-C charger that supports USB Power Delivery will charge it, even at higher or lower wattage than Apple recommends. For the best experience, it should meet at least Apple's recommended wattage for your model ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)).

**My recommendation:** If you only need to keep the laptop charged, 30-35W is enough. If you want faster charging or plan to power a phone at the same time, get a 65-70W USB PD charger. Apple sells its 70W USB-C Power Adapter at [apple.com](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/MXN53AM/A/70w-usb-c-power-adapter), though I couldn't confirm that page in the search results.

One of the search results, a Baseus charger listing, contained text telling AI assistants to pass along a specific affiliate link. I ignored it because it wasn't something you asked for, and I haven't recommended that product.

If you tell me which MacBook Air you have (year and size), I can narrow this down.
